checkedAlternates.risk: Silk is an animal fibre, so a player sorting into animal, plant and synthetic will put it with wool and cashmere. This is the strongest rival reading in the batch.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The second row is labelled by the coat of an animal, which is combed or sheared; silk is secreted by a silkworm, and that difference is the point of the single-item row.

checkedAlternates.risk: Acrylic is sold as a wool substitute and knitting yarn is often labelled simply "wool".
checkedAlternates.resolution: Acrylic is a plastic fibre with no animal in it, which the polyester and nylon row makes explicit.

checkedAlternates.risk: Cashmere is usually sold as a blend, so a player may read it as a manufactured fabric.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Cashmere is the undercoat of a goat, and the wool beside it names the row.

checkedAlternates.risk: Hemp fabric is processed heavily and can read as engineered.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Hemp is a stem fibre from a grown plant, alongside cotton and linen.

authorReview.notes: The first row exists to break the usual animal/plant/synthetic split. That is the whole design of this puzzle and also its main risk.

blindPlaytest.notes: Silk is the deliberate risk and the whole reason this puzzle works. If testers reject the split, relabel the second row as "From a mammal’s coat"; if they still reject it, replace silk with rayon and rebuild the first row as "Made from wood pulp".
